text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnia's fate is in its people hands who will decide if it will be partitioned or not once NATO-led peace forces are gone, newspaper commentary says.

- Deputy to international High Representative to Bosnia Michael Steiner warns political leaders and local media in the divided town of Mostar over hostile rhetorics which he said has aggravated tensions between rival Moslem and Croat communities.
- World Bank and European Bank for Reconstruction and Develpment shows that Bosnia's external debt at the beginning of 1996 was $3.23 billion.
- Klaus Muller, German embassy official in Sarajevo, says that Germans tried to encourage voluntary return of Bosnian refugees but at the end had to force them to leave Germany.
- A series of gold and silver coins to commemorate Pope John Paul II's visit to Bosnia on April 12 will be issued by Croat cultural society Napredak and Sarajevo branch of Croatian Gospodarska bank.
- Up to 30,000 worshippers are expected at a Mass which will be led by Pope John Paul II at Sarajevo's biggest soccer stadium on April 13, a Roman Catholic official says.
- A new Sarajevo mayor will be probably appointed by April 10, a Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) official says. The Bosnian capital has been without a mayor for more than a year.
- Air France in cooperation with Air Bosnia will start operating flights between Sarajevo and Paris via Zagreb soon, an Air France official says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
